nodes.label: LinterAPI facade
nodes.rationale: Single integration point that hides the L1/v2 split, owns the LRU cache + bounded executor, and exposes sync lint() + async lint_async(). Preserves L1+v2 semantics by calling the original lint_deck_combined() via a deferred import inside _run. Entry point for builder, chat tools, future LangChain agent, and tests.

nodes.label: LinterCache (OrderedDict LRU + Lock)
nodes.rationale: Bounded LRU (default 256) keyed on (path, content_sha256) with catalogue_version folded into the key by the caller (LinterAPI). Thread-safe via a single threading.Lock; move_to_end on read, popitem(last=False) on overflow. Returns deepcopy on get so callers can mutate safely. No timer, no TTL.

nodes.label: LinterExecutor (ThreadPoolExecutor + timeout)
nodes.rationale: Bounded worker pool (default 4) with timeout enforcement (default 30s). Sync submit() blocks on Future.result(timeout=...); async submit_async() uses loop.run_in_executor + asyncio.wait_for. Either path raises LinterTimeoutError on timeout and cancels the future so the worker is freed, never leaking the future.

nodes.label: LinterError (base exception)
nodes.rationale: Base class for all linter-API-level errors. Defined in executor.py and re-exported by api.py so callers catch a single taxonomy rather than the underlying parse exceptions.

nodes.label: LinterTimeoutError
nodes.rationale: Subclass of LinterError raised when a lint call exceeds the configured timeout budget. Raised by both sync submit() and async submit_async() after cancelling the underlying future.

nodes.label: CacheStats (frozen dataclass)
nodes.rationale: Frozen dataclass (hits, misses, size, evictions) returned by LinterCache.stats() and LinterAPI.cache_stats(). Exposed in the public surface for observability of cache behaviour.

nodes.label: lint_deck (package-level L1-only)
nodes.rationale: Bound from opm_ai.linter.linter (the original L1-only definition), NOT from opm_ai.linter.api. The api module also defines a lint_deck wrapper around default_api.lint (which runs L1+v2), so re-exporting the api one would silently switch L1-only callers to L1+v2. Keeping the package-level symbol L1-only preserves the 'ERROR blocks builder' contract and the v2-only delta assertions in test_lint_deck_combined_adds_v2_issues_when_they_fire.

nodes.label: api.lint_deck (facade wrapper, L1+v2)
nodes.rationale: Module-level shortcut defined in opm_ai/linter/api.py as def lint_deck(path): return default_api.lint(path). Runs L1+v2 through the executor pool. Exists for the explicit from opm_ai.linter.api import lint_deck use case (Task 2 pin test accepts either symbol). Must NOT be re-exported as the package lint_deck or it shadows the L1-only version.

nodes.label: lint_deck_combined (L1+v2)
nodes.rationale: Existing entry point that runs L1 then layers v2 checks. Lives in opm_ai/linter/linter.py. LinterAPI.lint() calls it via a deferred import inside _run to preserve L1+v2 semantics without recursion. Must keep working as a back-compat import throughout the refactor.

nodes.label: default_api (module-level LinterAPI instance)
nodes.rationale: Module-level singleton default_api = LinterAPI() in api.py. The canonical entry point for builder, chat tools, and tests; api.lint_deck is shorthand for default_api.lint.

nodes.label: catalogue_version()
nodes.rationale: Monotonically-increasing integer read from a frozen constant in opm_ai/linter/v2/catalogue/_version.py. Folded into the LinterCache key by LinterAPI._cache_key so any keywords.py regeneration self-invalidates every cache entry without a manual flush. The linter worker owns the bump (edits the file in the same commit that touches keywords.py). No edits to keywords.py happen in this plan.

nodes.label: bump_catalogue_version()
nodes.rationale: Test-only increment of catalogue_version. Must NOT be called from production code; the linter worker edits _version.py directly. Lets tests simulate a catalogue bump without modifying the real catalogue.

nodes.label: LintResult
nodes.rationale: Imported from opm_ai.linter.models. Cache stores LintResult and returns deepcopy on hit so two lint() calls on the same path return distinct mutable instances.

nodes.label: tool_lint_deck (chat route tool)
nodes.rationale: Chat-route tool in opm_ai/api/routes/chat.py migrated in Task 10 to call default_api.lint(...) instead of lint_deck_combined(...). No observable behaviour change.

nodes.label: builder.py linter callsites (L1-only, no-op migration)
nodes.rationale: Lines 394 and 430 of opm_ai/builder/builder.py call lint_deck() (L1-only), NOT lint_deck_combined() as Task 9 assumed. Switching them to default_api.lint() would silently move the builder from L1-only to L1+v2, violating 'ERROR blocks builder' and the plan's 'Output identical / No behaviour change' constraint. Task 9 was therefore closed as a documented no-op; the L1->L1+v2 switch needs its own future plan + test.

nodes.label: clear_deck_cache()
nodes.rationale: Defined in opm_ai/linter/linter.py. The linter module holds a process-local _DECK_CACHE keyed on (path, mtime_ns); across git checkout operations in the same Python process that cache can carry stale Deck instances from a previous commit and spuriously fail the v2-firing test. Task 8 prescribes calling clear_deck_cache() at the start of any debug session that flips between linter revisions.

nodes.label: _cache_key (path, sha256, catalogue_version)
nodes.rationale: LinterAPI._cache_key returns (str(path), sha256, catalogue_version()). Folding catalogue_version into the key means any catalogue regeneration self-invalidates the cache without manual flush. The plan's self-review noted lint() does a redundant second cache.get after put; the fix drops it but trades away the deepcopy-on-miss guarantee, documented as a future optimisation.

nodes.label: no-shim design (leave linter.py untouched)
nodes.rationale: Original plan asked for lint_deck_combined to become a shim calling default_api.lint(). That creates infinite recursion: default_api.lint -> _run -> lint_deck_combined -> default_api.lint -> ... until the 30s executor timeout fires, surfacing as LinterTimeoutError in every facade test. Fix: leave opm_ai/linter/linter.py byte-identical to baseline and only update __init__.py to re-export the new public types. default_api.lint already calls the original lint_deck_combined via a deferred import inside _run, preserving L1+v2 semantics with zero recursion risk. Side effect: the exports-only design means backwards compat is held entirely by __init__.py, which is where the package-level lint_deck shadowing pitfall lives.

nodes.label: api.lint_deck shadows package lint_deck pitfall
nodes.rationale: opm_ai.linter.api defines its own lint_deck wrapper around default_api.lint (L1+v2). If __init__.py re-exports it via `from opm_ai.linter.api import lint_deck`, the name opm_ai.linter.lint_deck becomes the facade-backed version, silently changing L1-only callers to L1+v2. This broke tests/unit/test_linter_combined.py::test_lint_deck_combined_adds_v2_issues_when_they_fire, which expects lint_deck(p) to have no L2xx codes and lint_deck_combined(p) to add them; both calls returned L1+v2 under the shadowing so the v2-only delta assertion failed. Fix: bind lint_deck from opm_ai.linter.linter (original L1-only definition), not from opm_ai.linter.api.

nodes.label: backwards-compatible import contract
nodes.rationale: `from opm_ai.linter import lint_deck, LintResult, LintIssue, lint_deck_combined, lint_deck_v2, Deck` MUST keep working throughout the refactor; Task 1 test #1 pins it. The new public surface (LinterAPI, LinterError, LinterTimeoutError, CacheStats, default_api) is additive only. Held by opm_ai/linter/__init__.py re-exporting both the original linter.py symbols and the new api.py symbols.

nodes.label: test_lint_deck_combined_adds_v2_issues_when_they_fire
nodes.rationale: Existing parity test in tests/unit/test_linter_combined.py that asserts lint_deck(p) yields no L2xx codes while lint_deck_combined(p) adds them. The api.lint_deck shadowing pitfall breaks this test because both calls return L1+v2; it is the regression sentinel that enforces keeping the package-level lint_deck L1-only.

hyperedges.label: LinterAPI facade wraps LinterCache + LinterExecutor + catalogue_version
L1 (lint_deck) vs L1+v2 (lint_deck_combined) layering enforced by shadowing test
exports-only refactor holds back-compat via __init__.py re-exports
